messages:
Alex Wu: Quick follow-up from the transport RFC — we need a concrete decision on iterator/cursor semantics across Python/TS/Go. Do we make resume tokens mandatory for paginated endpoints or provide a client-side fallback?
Jia Chen: I lean mandatory for server-backed cursors. If the server emits stable resume tokens we can guarantee no duplicates on retries. Otherwise clients get into messy dedupe territory.
Omar Malik: Mandatory tokens are ideal but not always possible for third-party backends. We should define a fallback strategy: client-managed checkpoint + at-least-once semantics and opt-in dedupe hooks.
Sasha Patel: Agreed. Proposal: expose ResumePolicy enum in SDKs: `ResumePolicy.Token | ResumePolicy.ClientCheckpoint | ResumePolicy.NoResume`. Default = Token when server supports it, else ClientCheckpoint.
Alex Wu: Nice. How does this interact with retries? If a retry replays a page request, and server isn't idempotent, we still risk duplicates. Need to tie retry window to resume policy.
Jia Chen: Right — add `retry.onNonIdempotent` behavior: fail-fast or use `transaction_id` header to force server-side idempotency when supported. SDK surface: allow `retry: { strategy, maxAttempts, onNonIdempotent }`.
Omar Malik: For transports: gRPC streaming can emit per-message checkpoints, HTTP long-poll can't. We should make transports advertise capabilities: `{resumeTokens: boolean, perMessageCheckpoint: boolean}` so higher layers pick strategy.
Sasha Patel: Example surface sketch (TS):
```ts
const it = client.listItems({ pageSize: 200 }, { resumePolicy: 'token', retry: { maxAttempts: 4, backoff: 'exp' } });
for await (const item of it) { /* ... */ }
// it.checkpoint() -> returns token when supported
```
Python:```py
it = client.list_items(page_size=200, resume_policy='token', retry={'max_attempts':4})
for item in it:
    ...
# it.checkpoint() -> token
```
Go:```go
it := client.ListItems(ctx, &ListOptions{PageSize:200}, WithResumePolicy(Token), WithRetry(MaxAttempts(4)))
for it.Next() { item := it.Item() /* ... */ }
// it.Checkpoint() // token or empty
```
Alex Wu: Good — keep the surfaces idiomatic per language. Also need low-level transport hooks so a custom transport can opt into token persistence and atomic ack semantics.
Jia Chen: Another important detail: memory/buffer controls. If client does ClientCheckpoint fallback it may need to buffer pages until checkpoint persisted. Add `maxBufferedPages` and `bufferFlushPolicy` options.
Omar Malik: Perf tradeoff: buffering increases latency and memory. For high-throughput endpoints default to `NoResume` with explicit user opt-in to checkpointing. For critical data paths default to Token.
Sasha Patel: Action items: 1) I'll draft an RFC follow-up with the ResumePolicy enum and transport capability matrix. 2) Jia/Omar will prototype the TS SDK iterator with token fallback and maxBufferedPages config. 3) Alex will list test cases (duplication, partial failure, cross-transport migration).
